hypotheses.observation: Within one species, pectoral fin area grows as SL^1.834 and wing loading as SL^1.236 (mass as SL^2.981): fin area falls behind the isometric square and wing loading outruns the isometric first power, so a bigger fish of the same species is more heavily loaded than isometry predicts.

scope.basis: Davenport 1992 (physics/allometry.json): within-species regressions on Exocoetus obtusirostris
scope.note: Three separate regressions, no confidence intervals, and NOT mutually consistent: 2.981 - 1.834 = 1.147 against the fitted 1.236. That inconsistency is why C13 needs intervals, and it is the reason nine audit rows read "violated" rather than a defect of those theorems.

lean.source:
/-- **The area law fails** under this observation: the exponent is not 2, so `AreaLaw` cannot hold with it. -/
theorem not_isometric_area (A : WithinSpeciesAllometry) : A.areaExponent ≠ 2 := by
  have := A.area_lt_isometric; intro h; rw [h] at this; exact absurd this (lt_irrefl 2)

named_hypotheses.name: Delphi.Empirical.WithinSpeciesAllometry
named_hypotheses.source:
/-- Fitted within-species exponents on standard length: fin area below the isometric 2, wing loading above
the isometric 1. The fields are the observation; the inequalities are what it says. -/
structure WithinSpeciesAllometry where
  areaExponent : ℝ
  wingLoadingExponent : ℝ
  massExponent : ℝ
  /-- Fin area grows more slowly than the square of length. -/
  area_lt_isometric : areaExponent < 2
  /-- Wing loading grows faster than length. -/
  loading_gt_isometric : 1 < wingLoadingExponent
  /-- Mass grows roughly as the cube. -/
  mass_near_cube : (2.9 : ℝ) ≤ massExponent ∧ massExponent ≤ 3.02
